newsitem.title: GERMANY: Clarke - G7 didn't see need for intervention accord.
newsitem.headline: Clarke - G7 didn't see need for intervention accord.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said the Group of Seven (G7) nations did not reach any agreement on concerted foreign exchange intervention at a meeting on Saturday.

"We reached no agreement of that kind today. We didn't think it was necessary," Clarke said in response to a question during an interview with Reuters Financial Television on the need for any intervention.
"We didn't think it necessary. We obviously all the time keep in touch between meetings, and we stand ready to act together in concert, if necessary. But that wasn't the situation today."
Clarke added that authorities did not want to try to control the foreign exchange market.
"The IMF (International Monetary Fund) doesn't seek to control the foreign exchange market," Clarke said.

"We don't have any set targets for the exchange rate of any currency. But we like the exchange rates to reflect the fundamentals," he said. "And we stand ready to act together in case we think that rates are moving out of line with the fundamentals."
